reasons: Lake treatment marks New York v. Class as good_law as of 2026-06-30.

reasons: Lake treatment marks Lewis v. United States as good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The scope note places Lewis in the settled misplaced-trust/false-friend line.
Lake treatment marks United States v. Karo as good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The scope note says the rule that monitoring a tracking device inside a private residence is a search remains controlling.
Lake treatment marks United States v. Place as good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The scope note says Caballes applied the luggage dog-sniff-is-not-a-search holding and Jardines is a context boundary, not an overruling.
Lake treatment marks Maryland v. Macon as good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The scope note confirms an undercover over-the-counter purchase of materials exposed for public sale is neither a search nor a seizure.
Lake treatment marks Illinois v. Caballes as good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The scope note says Rodriguez applies the no-prolongation principle and Jardines is a home-curtilage context boundary, not an overruling.
Lake treatment marks Berger v. New York as good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The scope note identifies Berger as the constitutional baseline for electronic-surveillance warrants.
Lake treatment marks United States v. Van Leeuwen as good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The scope note says brief detention of mailed packages on reasonable suspicion while a warrant is diligently sought is controlling law.
Lens B finds no treatment defect in the black-letter Katz rule: lake treatment marks Katz as good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The Katz scope note confirms the reasonable-expectation framework remains governing and that the revived trespass theory is additional, not substitutive.
residual_risks: Support and quote fidelity are outside Lens B and were not attacked here.
